    Indicator gene plots

    This submodule visualises the results of indicator_genes. The plot takes the results table as input, so the permutation test only has to be run once.

    Indicator gene heatmap

    Description

    Shows the strongest indicator genes of each group as rows and the groups as columns. Each cell is the fraction of the group's samples that carry the gene. Colour strips on the left indicate each metadata group, The cell for a gene's own group is its fidelity (B); how pale the rest of the row is reflects its specificity (A).

    Function

    heatmap 

    heatmap(pm, indicators, column, top_n=10, q_max=0.05, show_gene_labels=True)

    Plot the presence frequency of the top indicator genes in every group.

    Rows are the strongest indicator genes of each group, columns are the groups, and each cell is the fraction of that group's samples carrying the gene. Genes are grouped by the group they indicate, so a good indicator shows as a dark cell in its own group's column and pale cells elsewhere. The cell in a gene's own group equals its fidelity B. A colour strip on the left marks each row's indicator group, using the same colours as the other group plots.

    For each group, genes with q_value < q_max are ranked by stat (then by p_value and B to break ties) and the first top_n are shown. Groups with fewer significant genes show the ones they have.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    pm PavMatrix

    A PavMatrix instance.

    		 required
    indicators DataFrame

    The DataFrame returned by pavvis.stats.indicator.indicator_genes(pm, column, ...).

    		 required
    column str

    The discrete metadata column the indicators were computed for.

    		 required
    top_n int

    Maximum number of genes shown per group. Defaults to 10.

    		 10
    q_max float

    Genes are shown only if their q-value is below this. Defaults to 0.05.

    		 0.05
    show_gene_labels bool

    If True, label rows with gene IDs. Defaults to True.

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Figure

    A Plotly Figure. Call .show() to display or .write_html() to export.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If column is not a discrete metadata column, if indicators contains groups not in column or genes not in the PAV matrix, or if no gene has q_value < q_max.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    UserWarning

    If some groups have no gene with q_value < q_max.

    Example

    from pavvis import PavMatrix
from pavvis.stats.indicator import indicator_genes
import pavvis.plots.indicator as indicator_plots

pm = PavMatrix("path/to/pav.csv", "path/to/metadata.csv")
res = indicator_genes(pm, "clade", permutations=999, random_state=0)

indicator_plots.heatmap(pm, res, "clade", top_n=5).show()

    Interpretation

    A row dark in its own column and white elsewhere is a gene restricted to that group and carried by most of its samples. A row that is dark in its own column but also dark in others indicates a gene enriched in, but not restricted to, the group. A row that is pale everywhere but darkest in its own column is a rare but group-specific gene. Gene IDs can be long; set show_gene_labels=False for a compact overview when gene IDs do not mean anything.

    Specificity vs fidelity

    Description

    Plots the two components of the indicator value against each other for every significant indicator gene, with one panel per group. Specificity (A) is on the x-axis and fidelity (B) on the y-axis. Grey curves join points of equal IndVal.g statistic, so genes beyond the outer curve are the strongest indicators. Where the heatmap shows only the top genes, this plot shows all of them.

    Function

    specificity_fidelity 

    specificity_fidelity(
    pm, indicators, column, q_max=0.05, levels=(0.5, 0.7, 0.9), cols=4
)

    Plot specificity (A) against fidelity (B) of the significant indicator genes.

    One panel per group shows the genes with q_value < q_max assigned to that group. Genes in the upper right are carried by most of the group's samples and are rare elsewhere; high A with low B marks rare but group-restricted genes, and high B with lower A marks genes common in the group but shared with others. Grey curves mark equal IndVal.g statistic, sqrt(A * B) = level, and are labelled in the first panel.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    pm PavMatrix

    A PavMatrix instance.

    		 required
    indicators DataFrame

    The DataFrame returned by pavvis.stats.indicator.indicator_genes(pm, column, ...).

    		 required
    column str

    The discrete metadata column the indicators were computed for.

    		 required
    q_max float

    Genes are shown only if their q-value is below this. Defaults to 0.05.

    		 0.05
    levels tuple[float, ...]

    IndVal.g values drawn as reference curves. Pass () for none. Defaults to (0.5, 0.7, 0.9).

    		 (0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
    cols int

    Number of panels per row. Defaults to 4.

    		 4

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Figure

    A Plotly Figure. Call .show() to display or .write_html() to export.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If column is not a discrete metadata column, if indicators contains groups not in column or genes not in the PAV matrix, or if no gene has q_value < q_max.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    UserWarning

    If some groups have no gene with q_value < q_max.

    Example

    indicator_plots.specificity_fidelity(pm, res, "clade").show()

    Interpretation

    Genes in the upper right are carried by most samples of the group and rarely occur elsewhere. Genes on the right but low down on the plot are rare, yet almost restricted to the group. Genes at the top of the plot but further left are common in the group and also common in others. A group whose cloud sits far to the right has a distinctive gene content.
